title: Transactions and Concurrency: ACID, Locks, and Isolation

questions.question: A transfer transaction debits account A and then crashes before crediting account B. Which ACID property guarantees A's money is restored?
questions.rationale: Atomicity makes the transaction all-or-nothing: the partial work is rolled back via the undo log, so the debit disappears along with the failed credit. Durability only protects committed work.

questions.question: T2 reads a balance that T1 has updated but not yet committed, and then T1 rolls back. T2 has just made a:
questions.rationale: A dirty read is reading uncommitted data — here a value that vanishes when T1 rolls back. READ COMMITTED and above prevent it.

questions.question: T2 runs the same range query twice and, between the two executions, T1 inserts a matching row that now appears in the results. Which anomaly is this?
questions.rationale: A phantom read is new rows appearing in a repeated predicate-based query. A non-repeatable read changes an existing row's value instead; only SERIALIZABLE fully prevents phantoms.

questions.question: What is the weakest SQL isolation level that prevents non-repeatable reads?
questions.rationale: READ COMMITTED still allows rereads of a row to differ, REPEATABLE READ pins each row's first-seen version — it is the lowest level that stops non-repeatable reads (though phantoms can persist).

questions.question: Two transactions both request a shared (S) lock on the same row. What happens?
options: Both are granted, since readers do not conflict with readers
The second waits until the first commits
The engine escalates both to exclusive locks
questions.rationale: Shared locks are compatible with each other — many concurrent readers may hold them. Only a shared-versus-exclusive or exclusive-versus-exclusive combination conflicts.

questions.question: Under two-phase locking, what does the shrinking phase mean?
options: The transaction locks fewer rows than it reads
The transaction releases locks early to help others
After releasing its first lock, the transaction may acquire no new locks
The engine automatically downgrades exclusive locks to shared
questions.rationale: 2PL splits a transaction into a growing phase of acquisitions and a shrinking phase of releases; no new lock may be acquired after the first release, which is what makes the schedule serialisable.

questions.question: Requiring every transaction to acquire locks in a fixed global order (always A before B) prevents deadlock by eliminating which condition?
questions.rationale: With a single global ordering, a cycle in the wait-for graph cannot form — circular wait is the Coffman condition most cheaply attacked, since the others are inherent to locking.

questions.question: What is the headline benefit of MVCC (multiversion concurrency control)?
options: It eliminates the need for a write-ahead log
It raises the isolation level to SERIALIZABLE automatically
Readers never block writers and writers never block readers
questions.rationale: MVCC keeps multiple row versions so each transaction reads a consistent snapshot while writers add new versions — readers and writers proceed without waiting on each other; deadlocks and logging are separate concerns.

questions.question: Which statement states the write-ahead logging (WAL) rule?
options: Data pages must reach disk before the log
The log record describing a change must reach stable storage before the changed data page
Logs are written only at checkpoints
COMMIT may return before the log is flushed
questions.rationale: Durability works because the log reaches stable storage first: after a crash, recovery can redo committed work from the log even though the data pages were still dirty in the buffer pool.

questions.question: Compared with READ COMMITTED, SERIALIZABLE isolation additionally prevents:
options: Phantom reads, plus all other anomaly combinations
questions.rationale: SERIALIZABLE is the top of the ladder: it guarantees transactions behave as if executed one at a time, eliminating dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, phantoms, and every other interleaving anomaly.
